conventions.convention: One-tape heads range over the natural numbers; an L-move at 0 remains at 0, and an S-move leaves the head unchanged.
The ordinary simulator represents an original state q by unmarked (q,0), uses marked (q,1) only as the interior of an S macro, and only unmarked designated states halt.
A computation count counts genuine transitions only; an already-halting start has count zero, not an identity-extended tail.
Semigroup equality is finite symmetric contextual replacement in A-plus; augmented configurations permit an empty right tape exactly at the stopping state q_0.
For a signed tape word, sharp reverses each letter sign without reversing letter order; special words have positive, possibly empty tape contexts X,Y and are spelled X-sharp q_j Y.
AC is assumed for the HNN normal-form and transversal arguments, while the normalized-machine and semigroup construction are choice-free.

load_bearing.statement: Defines stay-put one-tape machines, their clamped-left-boundary one-step relation, and unique finite or infinite maximal runs.
The right-left tagged-state macro simulates exactly one stay-put step, in both directions between successive unmarked configurations.
There is a fixed finite normalized deterministic machine T whose sole stopping state is reached on v(w) exactly when the fixed HALT recognizer accepts w.
Defines the fixed positive semigroup Gamma encoding T, its augmented configurations, terminal q, and initial word C(w).
For every binary word w, C(w)=q in Gamma if and only if T stops on v(w).
Defines the finite Boone presentation B, sharp, positive special words Sigma, Sigma-star, and W(Sigma).
Assuming AC, establishes the required free base groups, associated free subgroups and edge isomorphisms, together with the finite multiple-letter Britton interface.
Assuming AC, constructs the embedded HNN tower G_0≤G_2≤G_3≤B and identifies the auxiliary subgroups needed for the two stable-letter stages.
Assuming AC, L Sigma R=q in G_2 for a special word forces Sigma-star=q in the positive semigroup Gamma.
Assuming AC, for every positive special word Sigma, W(Sigma)=1 in B if and only if Sigma-star=q in Gamma.
One fixed finite positive semigroup presentation has undecidable equality C(w)=q on its encoded initial words.
Assuming AC, there exists one fixed finite presentation whose word problem is undecidable.

concerns.concern: The claim calls T a deterministic machine on a two-sided tape with exactly one stopping state, while its cited local machine interface is right-infinite, clamped at zero, and has two designated halting states. The proof gives a workable transition-table construction, but does not formally define the altered one-stop/two-sided machine class or explicitly prove that its finite-description interface is the one subsequently required by the semigroup construction.
